definition: A join combines rows from two tables by a related value, usually a foreign key matching a primary key. An inner join keeps only pairs that match. A left join keeps every row of the left table and fills nulls when the right side has no match.
prompt: What is a join in SQL?
details: A right join keeps every row of the right table. A full join keeps rows from both sides. A cross join pairs every row of one table with every row of the other.
examples: Orders joined to customers on customer id
Users left-joined to profiles so users without a profile still appear
